title: Bought assets never matched, and asking people to fix again felt rude. AI solved both (and it never sighs)
author: bakacandy
selftext:
Hello, I am solo developer from Korea. English is not my language so I used translator. If something is strange, it is translator's fault. Translator is also AI, so it is AI's fault again.



This is Dock 7. It is cozy 2D pixel game. You live in half-moon station that goes around the moon, cut old ships with laser, and bring home the things left inside. Tapes, letters, things people left behind. Also there is a cat. Demo is coming to Steam in December.



I wanted to make this game, but I had two problems. First, assets. One asset never has everything I need, and when I mix many assets, every part looks like it came from a different game. Second, people. I thought about working with someone, but asking "can you fix this again?" for the 5th time felt rude to me. So I just could not.



AI solved both. Everything comes from one place so the style stays same. And I can say "fix it again" 10 times, 40 times, and AI never sighs. (I think.) With AI help, finally it is going to the direction I wanted. Code, pixel art, writing and translation is Claude (Claude Code, Unity 6), music is Suno. It is written on Steam page too.



But there is a catch. AI is very fast, but it does not know where I want to go. It suggests the same idea again and again, very politely. So I keep a "rejected list" in the rules file that AI reads every session. Now about 40 lines. Dark hull. Parallax. Harpoon. Bigger drill. The saddest one was a drone that cuts the wreck by itself. I liked it, until I noticed I was just watching the game play itself. Sorry drone.



Rules file grows same way. When AI repeats a mistake, it becomes a rule. My favorite: AI started answering me in English at the end of long work. I told it 3 times. Now it is a rule. (This post is in English. Please don't tell it.)



Also a few Claude sessions share one Unity editor and wait in a queue, like office printer. One time one session called a secret editor function and the editor died for everyone. That is a rule too now.



Question for people doing similar thing: how do you keep your direction when AI keeps bringing back ideas you already killed? My list works but it keeps getting longer.

comments.author: Nicolas-Gauge
comments.body: Looks great. Reject lists are good as long as they are specific enough not to reject the wrong things. Trying to explain the outcomes you want can be very helpful too.

replies.author: bakacandy
replies.body: Good point. I will try to make the rules more specific. Thanks!

comments.author: ItsDumi
comments.body:
Smaller prompts for me. I don't ask it to make a whole system, I will have it make a function or 2, integrate, and then make another function or 2. Step by step, so I iterate when I want to and if it do too much I can take 1 step back without reprompt everything. 

Also I don't ask AI for idea, when I need ideas I tell it to give me questions/constraints so that I come up with the idea. I use it to prompt me. So I consider many details I might miss.
